Founding year 1997 is from company boilerplate carried in third-party listings, not the current site. description: Utility billing and customer information software for small and mid-size municipal water, sewer, and multi-service utilities
notes: Legal name Continental Utility Solutions, Inc.; the site brands as CUSI and says "nearly four decades" without a year - 1984 comes from the company's own third-party profiles. Serves 1,150+ utilities.

description: Customer information, billing, and mobile workforce software for public power, water, and gas utilities
notes: Owned by Harris Computer Systems, a Constellation Software subsidiary; NorthStar was Harris's original business unit. Sibling company to Advanced Utility Systems and inHANCE in this same batch - all three are Harris-owned CIS vendors.

description: Pump station control and optimization analytics for municipal water and wastewater utilities
notes: Products are Tagger, Dynamic Pump Optimizer, and Lift Station Guardian; founding year 2010 is from third-party profiles, not the site

description: CAMA mass appraisal, property tax billing and collection, appeals, and assessment analytics software for county assessors and tax offices
notes: Legal name Farragut Systems, Inc.; product family is Arist (CAMA, GIS, Appeals, Analytics) and they run the statewide NCPTS system for North Carolina counties. Site claims 30+ years but states no founding year, so omitted. They also sell a workers' compensation line to insurance carriers - a secondary, non-government market.

description: Pension, unemployment insurance, paid family leave, and workforce program administration systems for state government agencies
notes: Products are Neospin (pension), Neosurance (UI/PFML/disability), WorkforceNXT, HealConnect, and Neotrient, all on their Xelence platform. Categorized under Workforce & Labor because UI and labor agencies are the NASWA-facing business, but the pension administration line would sit under General Gov / HR & Workforce. Registered address is Little Canada, MN in the Saint Paul metro.

description: Community engagement and stakeholder relationship management platform for councils, transportation agencies, and infrastructure project owners
notes: New unified brand combining the Social Pinpoint and Consultation Manager products; dual headquarters in Vancouver, BC and Brisbane, Australia (I recorded Vancouver). No founding year published for the Open Point entity, so omitted. Resources and mining is a listed secondary industry alongside government and transportation.

description: Commercial off-the-shelf systems for state tax and revenue, child support, unemployment insurance, and motor vehicle agencies
notes: Candidate was flagged for FastCSE (child support), which would sit under Health & Human Services / Child & Family Services; categorized on the dominant product instead - GenTax tax administration, used by 60+ revenue agencies. FastCore now backs 100+ government programs. HQ and founding year are from their about page as surfaced in search; fastenterprises.com's homepage states neither.

description: Library, technology asset, and facilities management software for K-12 school districts
notes: Renamed from Follett School Solutions in August 2024; flagship product is Destiny Library Manager. No founding year is published for the software business (parent Follett Corporation dates to 1873 as a bookseller, which would be misleading on this card), so year_founded omitted.

description: Canvas learning management system plus assessment and credentialing software for universities, school districts, and government training programs
notes: Exhibited at a K-12 conference and the candidate URL was the /k12 page; sectored to Higher Education because Canvas's dominant installed base is colleges and universities - K-12 districts are a large second market, so K-12 Schools / Operations & SIS is a defensible alternative. Acquired by KKR in 2024; also owns Mastery Connect and Parchment.

description: Zero-trust student data exchange, SSO, and app privacy governance for K-12 districts and their edtech vendors
notes: Formerly Global Grid for Learning (GG4L). HQ and founding year are from third-party company profiles, not the site. Half the customer base is edtech vendors rather than districts.

description: Classroom communication and engagement app connecting K-12 teachers, students, and families
notes: Judgment call for the owner: the product is K-12-specific and used in public schools, but their press page says it is "100% free for schools" - revenue comes from family subscriptions (ClassDojo Plus, Dojo Tutor) and venture funding, so there is no district sales motion in the usual govtech sense. Candidate had no URL; classdojo.com confirmed, HQ from the address in their privacy policy. Founding year not stated anywhere on the site, so omitted.

description: Cloud security, content filtering, and student safety monitoring for Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 in K-12 districts
notes: Products are Cloud Monitor, Content Filter (CIPA), and Classroom Manager. Categorized under School Safety because the pitch pairs cybersecurity with student self-harm and bullying signal detection; K-12 Schools / Operations & SIS would also fit since the buyer is the district technology leader.

description: Income and work-hours verification (Income Passport) for state SNAP, Medicaid, and human services eligibility staff
notes: HQ taken from the address in their privacy policy; no founding year appears anywhere on the site, so omitted. Explicitly positioned as built for human services agencies, unlike the horizontal verification vendors.

description: Prepaid card issuance and funds disbursement platform for guaranteed income, disaster relief, and benefits programs
notes: givecard.io redirects to givecard.com. Government and nonprofit benefit programs are the anchor use cases, but they also serve businesses paying employees and research participants - close to the scope_review line. No founding year published, so omitted.

description: Web-based tenant, property, and financial management software for public housing authorities
notes: PHA-Web is the product brand of Management Computer Services, Inc. The site references operating since 2003 without stating a company founding year, so year_founded omitted. Claims to serve over 25% of US housing authorities.

description: AI contact center, intake automation, and patient engagement software for behavioral health providers
notes: No headquarters is stated on the site - a linked Psychology Today listing suggests Anchorage, AK but that is a clinician directory entry, not a company address, so hq_location omitted. Buyers are community behavioral health organizations and treatment providers, many publicly funded (they cite high-risk Medicaid patients).

description: Crisis response, closed-loop referral, care management, and bed board software for behavioral health agencies
notes: Named buyers include state and county health agencies, community behavioral health organizations, and FQHCs. No founding year published on the site, so omitted.

description: AI session transcription, fidelity scoring, and training feedback for behavioral health, crisis lines, and human services agencies
notes: Named buyers include state and local governments, CCBHCs, health systems, and payors. No headquarters address or founding year appears on the site (about, company, and privacy pages all yield nothing), so both omitted.

description: AI simulated-patient platform for clinical skill building and supervision in behavioral health workforces
notes: Thin site - essentially a product blurb and a contact form. It names "healthcare organizations" rather than public agencies, so the public-sector buyer is inferred from the NatCon exhibit rather than confirmed; worth a second look. No HQ or founding year published (the /about path returns Access Denied).

description: Case management, intake, referral, and grant tracking software for public and nonprofit human services programs
notes: Spans HMIS, workforce development, foster care, veterans services, housing, behavioral health, and disaster relief - too broad for any single HHS subcategory, so filed under the General Gov / Health & Human Services pair. No founding year published.

description: Human services EHR and care coordination software for behavioral health, residential, vocational rehab, and food assistance providers
notes: Holding company for AxiomEHR, Foothold AWARDS, SaraWorks, and Link2Feed; serves 14,000+ care providers in the US and Canada. No founding year published on the site.

description: Contingency-management incentive and engagement app for outpatient behavioral health and substance use programs
notes: Serves clinics, CCBHCs, and Medicaid SMI/SUD programs. No HQ or founding year anywhere on the site (about and contact paths 404), so both omitted. Unrelated to the former Verity Health System hospital chain - confirmed by the product content at verityhealth.io.

description: Event calendar, room booking, museum pass, and Library of Things modules for public library websites
notes: Small two-principal shop; no founding year published, so omitted

description: Evidence-based collection analytics and management software for public and academic libraries
notes: collectionHQ Ltd., registered in Scotland (No. 849460). Site cites 21+ years of the underlying methodology but states no founding year, and discloses no parent company, so both omitted. Serves 8,000+ public library branches across the UK, Ireland, US, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

description: Phonics and decodable-text literacy platform for library reading programs, K-4 classrooms, and families
notes: Literacy Leap is the product; the footer names Chronicle LLC as the operating entity and shows a 301 (Maryland) phone number while the origin story points to St. Louis - too conflicting to record an HQ, so omitted, as is the unpublished founding year. Category is the buyer channel (PLA/libraries); K-12 Schools would fit the classroom market equally well since the sector map has no instructional-content bucket.

description: Interactive multimedia ebook collections for K-12 classrooms and public libraries
notes: Candidate had no URL, and lightboxlearning.com is a parked domain that JavaScript-redirects to a /lander page - the live site is openlightbox.com, confirmed by the Lightbox Learning branding and founder Linda Weigl's letter. No founding year published. Same category caveat as Decodable Reads: content product sold into both the library and school channels.

description: Web-based mapping, demographic, and consumer data visualization application for university and public library patrons
notes: Named customers are academic libraries (Berkeley, Princeton, Stanford, McGill) and public libraries (NYPL, Charlotte Mecklenburg). No address or founding year is published anywhere on the site - about, contact, and privacy paths all 404 - so both omitted. Could equally sit under Higher Education / IT & Administration given the academic library base.

description: Campus software delivery and virtual application access platform for university IT and computer labs
notes: Contact page lists a US office at 307 W Tremont Ave, Charlotte, NC and a UK office near Leeds; recorded the UK office as HQ since the operating entity is British, but confirm which the owner wants on the card. Site says "15 years" without a founding year, so year_founded omitted.

description: Multi-model collaborative AI workspace for university and college faculty, staff, and students
notes: Higher education and community colleges lead the customer list, but they also sell to enterprise teams, nonprofits, and individuals - a step toward horizontal, worth watching. No HQ or founding year published (about, contact, and privacy paths return nothing).

description: Managed SAML and CAS identity federation, SSO, and guest-identity services for higher education institutions
notes: Squarely higher-ed-only: community colleges, R1s, state systems, and research organizations. Founding year is stated on their about page; no headquarters address appears anywhere on the site, so hq_location omitted.

description: Brightspace learning management system for universities, school districts, and government training programs
notes: Also sells Brightspace to corporate and association customers, so there is a horizontal edge, but education is clearly the core. The site says "just over 25 years" rather than naming a year; 1999 is D2L's own consistently published founding date.

description: Discussion board, peer review, and document annotation tools that plug into university LMS courses
notes: Used by 200+ universities including Michigan, Brown, and Fayetteville State. The site returns 403 to WebFetch (read via curl with a Chrome user agent); HQ is the address in the site footer. An about page carries "Since 2008" but it is not clearly a founding statement, so year_founded omitted.

description: Managed higher education data lake, lakehouse, and generative AI advising tools built on campus SIS, LMS, CRM, and ERP data
notes: Products are InvokeUnify, InvokeClarity, and AlterEgo; explicitly higher-education-only. No founding year published.

description: AI student support, tutoring, grading, and operations assistants for universities and colleges
notes: 200+ institutions from community colleges to research universities; no founding year published on the site

description: Higher education integration and AI platform (LightLeapAI) for campus data quality, document processing, and enrollment fraud detection
notes: Started as an integration services firm and now states plainly that it is a platform company, not a services shop - worth re-checking if the owner sorts on services revenue. 500+ institutions.

description: AI and VR public speaking simulator for university communication courses and professional training
notes: Educators at universities and institutions lead the customer framing, but they also sell to business professionals and individual learners, so there is a consumer and corporate edge. No HQ or founding year published on the site.

description: Skills, career readiness, and portfolio assessment platform for universities and their students
notes: Trusted by 50+ universities; UK-based (British spelling throughout, exhibits at BETT London) but no registered address appears on the site and the /about and /contact-us paths 404, so hq_location and year_founded are both omitted.

description: Attendance, engagement, academic scheduling, exams, and visa compliance platform for universities and colleges
notes: Legal entity SEAtS Software Ltd. Site returns 403 to WebFetch (read via curl with a Chrome user agent). Lists offices in London, Dublin, Texas, and Sydney without naming a headquarters, and publishes no founding year, so both fields omitted. Also sells to further education and K-12.

description: Web content management, course catalog, and student portal software for university marketing and recruitment teams
notes: Site names "The Academy, 42 Pearse Street, Dublin" as worldwide headquarters. The only date on the site is a 2016-2026 copyright range, which is not a founding year, so year_founded omitted.

description: AI career readiness, resume, and outcomes tracking platform for university career services offices
notes: 58+ college and university customers; also sells to nonprofits, workforce development programs, and job boards. No founding year published.

description: Institutional performance analytics, cost analytics, and assessment software for colleges and universities
notes: Spun out of the University of Maryland Global Campus Office of Analytics; customer base is higher-ed institutions including public systems.

description: School and college search data platform selling enrollment marketing and direct admissions to universities and K-12 districts
notes: Site is behind a PerimeterX block for both WebFetch and curl; facts confirmed from Wikipedia, Crunchbase News, and Pittsburgh Technology Council coverage. Founded 2002 as College Prowler, renamed Niche in 2013. Judgment call: they run a data/lead platform but also market themselves as an enrollment marketing agency, so the product-vs-services line is worth a second look.

description: AI noise monitoring sensors and evidence reporting for councils, environment departments, and other noise regulators
notes: No URL was supplied; found via search at noisenet.com (also noisenet.com.au). Category is a judgment call - noise-nuisance complaint handling sits between citizen services and code enforcement, and their Animal Care Expo presence is about barking-dog complaints.

description: Property tax escrow, bulk payment, and payment processing platform for county and municipal tax offices
notes: Legal entity is Autoagent Data Solutions, LLC; the site brands as Autoagent.

description: Permitting, code enforcement, land use, and request management software for municipalities, townships, and counties
notes: Brands itself SDL on the site; the legal/LinkedIn name is Spatial Data Logic. Site claims 26+ years but names no founding year, so the year is omitted. 260+ local government clients.

description: Outage notification, billing, and omnichannel customer communication platform for investor-owned, municipal, and cooperative utilities
notes: Legal name Convey, LLC; rebranded from Message Broadcast. Utilities are the lead market but the platform is also sold into finance, healthcare, insurance, and telecom, so a horizontal read is defensible. No founding year on the site.

description: Road and bridge project development software covering estimating, electronic bidding, construction management, and materials testing for state DOTs, counties, and municipalities
notes: No URL was supplied; found at exevision.com. The candidate vertical said "asset and permit software" - that describes iWorQ Systems, a different Utah local-gov vendor, not ExeVision, whose products are iPDWeb, iCXWeb, and eFieldbook for transportation projects (fits NACE, the county engineers show). Founding year left blank: the site says "since 2005" for transportation work while third-party profiles say the company was founded in 1994.

description: Family caregiver education and support platform licensed by Area Agencies on Aging, state aging units, and health plans
notes: Site blocks WebFetch and curl (CleanTalk bot protection); deployment confirmed via dozens of live agency-branded subdomains (e.g. coaaa.trualta.com, aaaphx.trualta.com). HQ appears as Toronto in most profiles and Ottawa in one, so treat the city as lightly held.

description: Risk and needs assessment, case planning, and case management software for county probation, juvenile justice, and correctional agencies
notes: No founding year published on the site.

description: Cloud diversion program management, eLearning, citation processing, and document management for prosecutors, probation, and police agencies
notes: Site brands the company "Adventfs" and its products "Advent"; flagship is Diversion Manager (diversionmanager.com). HQ from third-party business profiles - the contact page lists no address - so treat the city as lightly held. No founding year found.

description: AquaTwin digital twin software for water and sewer hydraulic modeling, surge analysis, and asset management, sold to water utilities and engineering consultants
notes: Esri partner; product line is AquaTwin Water, Sewer, Surge, Asset, and HCM. No founding year published on the site or in the profiles found.

description: Capital program and construction project management software for infrastructure owners including federal, state, and local agencies
notes: FedRAMP authorized since 2022; named public customers include the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission. Also sells to commercial, healthcare, and education owners, so a horizontal read is arguable, but the product is construction-vertical rather than general-purpose.

description: Springboard utility billing, customer information, and field operations software for electric, water, and municipal utilities
notes: Goes by PCS. Site claims 40+ years but names no founding year, so the year is omitted.

description: Automated text, voice, email, and mail notification software that turns AMI meter data into leak alerts and service outage messages for water utilities
notes: HQ and founding year omitted: several unrelated companies named Spout appear in the business databases and none could be matched to spoutservices.com with confidence, while the site itself publishes no address.

description: Operations data logging, sampling, and regulatory compliance reporting software for water and wastewater systems
notes: Products are Rounds, Assets, and Samples. HQ and year come from third-party profiles; the site's contact page still shows placeholder address text.

description: AI browser extension that generates lesson plans, quizzes, and student feedback inside Google Workspace and LMS tools for teachers and school districts
notes: Sells to individual teachers and to districts (site claims 20,000 districts); $5M seed led by Owl Ventures 2024, $15M Series A led by Bessemer 2025. HQ omitted: funding coverage puts it in San Francisco, other profiles in Los Altos, CA, and the site publishes no address.

description: Cyber readiness platform for schools and trusts covering security scoring, phishing simulation, policy building, staff training, and penetration testing
notes: UK-founded (by a former headteacher and a compliance specialist) and acquired by Wonde in August 2022; runs a US site at /en-us, which fits the CoSN listing. HQ omitted - sources split between Middlesbrough and Newmarket, UK, and the site names no city. Category is a judgment call: the map has no K-12 IT/cyber bucket, so this sits under School Safety.

description: SaaS state-based health insurance marketplace and eligibility platform for Medicaid, SNAP, child care, and unemployment programs
notes: Vimo, Inc. operates the GetInsured brand; runs state-based marketplaces for roughly ten states. Founding year from the company's own August 2025 "20 years" press release. The vimo.com site is JavaScript-rendered and returns almost nothing to WebFetch or curl, so details came from Vimo/GetInsured press releases.

description: Natural language processing software that surfaces risks and insights from caseworker case notes for child welfare and behavioral health agencies
notes: Legal name Augmented Intelligence Technologies, Inc. Public deployments include Allegheny County and Washington County, PA and Illinois DCFS. HQ omitted: coverage variously calls it a Pittsburgh and a Chicago company and the site lists no address. No founding year published.

description: CaseWorks enterprise content management and workflow automation for state, county, and tribal health and human services agencies
notes: Goes by NCT. Acquired by Banyan Software (Toronto) in June 2021; still operates as its own product line. Editions cover child support, child welfare, financial/eligibility services, workforce, and adult services.

description: Accounting, occupancy, Section 8, maintenance, and tenant management software for public housing authorities
notes: No URL was supplied; found at sacssoftware.com. Operating name of Scott Accounting & Computer Services, Inc. (sacsinc.com). Founding year 1969 comes from the company LinkedIn profile, not the website, so treat it as lightly held. Covers Public Housing, HCV, LIHTC, Multifamily, and Rural Development programs.

description: LOCUS Online level-of-care assessment software and EHR integrations for behavioral health providers, payers, and public health agencies
notes: LOCUS (Level of Care Utilization System for Psychiatric and Addiction Services) is the standardized instrument many state behavioral health authorities require; the site names public health entities among its buyers, which is why this reads govtech rather than commercial healthcare. No founding year published.

description: Business and consumer reference and marketing database licensed to public libraries, academic institutions, and government agencies for patron job search and small business research
notes: Operated by DatabaseUSA; the About page describes it as founded by Vin Gupta after he left Infogroup, whose sale it dates to 2010, but it never states AtoZdatabases' own founding year, so the year is omitted. No street address published on the site.

description: Cloud suite for libraries covering website CMS, event and room booking, appointments, digital signage, mobile apps, kiosks, and discovery search
notes: 400+ library customers. The site claims 20 years established but gives no founding year, and its contact page returned nothing usable, so HQ and year are both omitted.

description: Reference databases, streaming video, and career research content licensed to K-12 schools, colleges, public libraries, and employers
notes: Brands include Facts On File, Films On Demand, Credo, and Vault. Founding year omitted: the site's timeline starts at 1941 for Facts On File, but Infobase as an entity is later and undated. HQ omitted: the only address on the contact page is 8 The Green, Suite 19225, Dover, DE, which reads as a registered-agent address rather than an operating HQ.

description: Digitized archive of legal, legislative, and government documents licensed by subscription to law, academic, and public libraries
notes: LLMC is a nonprofit library consortium (Law Library Microform Consortium) selling memberships to its database rather than a commercial vendor - worth the owner's eye on whether nonprofits belong on cards. Branding references a 50th anniversary, implying roughly 1976, but no founding year is stated, so it is omitted.

description: Integrated library system, discovery, and mobile software for public, academic, school, and government libraries
notes: Year is the 2005 Sirsi/Dynix merger that created the current company; the predecessors date to 1979 (Sirsi) and 1983 (Dynix), so the owner may prefer an earlier date. Serves 23,000+ library facilities in 70+ countries.

description: Student success analytics and case management platform that predicts and tracks persistence and completion for colleges and universities
notes: Founding year stated on the company's own about page. Named customers include University of Cincinnati, Texas A&M, and Wayne State - public institutions.

description: Higher education data lakehouse with warehouse, catalog, lineage, governance, semantic modeling, and BI layers for institutional reporting
notes: Site is fully JavaScript-rendered and returns only the title tag to WebFetch and curl; the product scope above is reconstructed from the sitemap (platform, warehouse, catalog, lineage, governance, semantic, bi, ai, ingestion, dbt, multi-tenant). No about or contact content was retrievable, so HQ and year are omitted and the description is coarser than the others - worth a human look.

description: AI-native CRM and Bolt AI agents for higher education admissions, marketing, student success, and continuing education teams
notes: HQ stated on the company's own about page; 350+ institutions. No founding year published.

description: Alumni engagement, mentoring, student support chatbots, and donor fundraising software for colleges, universities, K-12 schools, and nonprofits
notes: Product family is Graduway, Ivy, Ocelot, Raise, and Advance; 2,750+ institutions. Shape resembles the Blackbaud case the owner flagged - education-plus-nonprofit advancement rather than pure govtech - so it may belong in scope_review instead. HQ is the address published in the site footer. No founding year published.

description: AI plus live online exam proctoring integrated with learning management systems for universities and K-12 schools
notes: About page describes founding by two Florida Atlantic University students but gives no year, and no address is published, so both fields are omitted.

description: Scaffold platform for LMS migration, course archiving, and data warehousing across LMS, SIS, and CRM systems at colleges and universities
notes: Named customers include UCLA, USC, Texas Tech, and UMass Amherst. No founding year published.

description: Planning, outcomes assessment, accreditation, and program review software for colleges, universities, and higher education systems
notes: No founding year published on the site.

description: LockDown Browser, Respondus Monitor proctoring, and exam authoring software for universities and K-12 schools
notes: respondus.com 301-redirects to web.respondus.com. Site says "pioneer of online testing for two decades" but gives no founding year, and publishes no address, so both are omitted. Embedded in 70+ third-party assessment platforms.

description: AI-assisted grading that produces first-pass scores and feedback on papers, technical work, and video assignments against instructor rubrics
notes: Claims 1,300+ institutions including Arizona State, University of Illinois, Dartmouth, and McGill. No HQ or founding year published on the site.

description: Video platform, digital accessibility scanning and document remediation, and test proctoring for universities, school districts, and government institutions
notes: Also sells into healthcare and finance, so a horizontal read is arguable, but education is clearly the primary market. HQ omitted: the about page says only "legal headquarters in Delaware with primary U.S. offices in Silicon Valley, California" and names no city. No founding year published.

description: Wi-Fi-based space occupancy analytics and planning software for colleges and universities
notes: Formerly Degree Analytics; rebranded to CampusIQ. Site footer shows the legal entity as MF Genius, Corp.

description: Campus ID credentialing, tuition and dining payments, access control and foodservice software for colleges, universities and hospitals
notes: Rebrand of Transact + CBORD, completed March 2026; a Roper Technologies subsidiary. transactcampus.com and cbord.com still redirect/coexist during the transition. Exhibited under the transitional 'Transact + CBORD' name.

description: Digital textbook and courseware delivery platform used by colleges, universities and their publishers
notes: Site blocks automated fetches (Cloudflare 403); details confirmed from Wikipedia, CB Insights and Library Technology Guides profiles. Judgment call: a large share of revenue comes from publishers rather than institutions directly, though inclusive-access programs are sold to campuses.

description: Animal intake, medical, foster and adoption record software for animal shelters and rescue organizations
notes: Buyer base is mixed: municipal animal-control shelters plus a large share of nonprofit foster-based rescues. No founding year found on the site or in Crunchbase-style sources.

description: Cloud customer information, billing and field service software for municipal water, sewer, electric and gas utilities
notes: No founding year stated on the site. Category is the closest fit in the map: the product is a utility-wide CIS spanning water and electric, not grid hardware.

description: Menu planning, production record and performance analytics software for K-12 school nutrition departments
notes: menulogic-k12.com 301-redirects to menulogic.io. Site footer names the operating entity Foodworks Technologies, LLC. No HQ or founding year found on the site, Tracxn, or LinkedIn.

description: Legal case and matter management software for prosecutors, public defenders, city and county attorneys, school districts and tribal governments
notes: Acquired in 2024 by Waxman Ventures and rolled up with Judicial Dialog Systems (founded 1994) and Cycom Data Systems (founded 1984); HQ moved from the original Philadelphia location to North Canton, OH. Founded year 1989 is LegalEdge's own, from its About page.

description: Family caregiver burnout assessment and care-plan platform for Medicaid agencies, area agencies on aging, health plans and long-term care insurers
notes: Founding year not on their own site; 2014 is from CB Insights and PitchBook profiles, though one press interview describes a 2017 launch, so treat the year as soft. Delivery pairs the software with staffed care specialists.

description: Fair-chance job matching and reentry platform for corrections agencies, probation and parole departments, reentry nonprofits and background-friendly employers
notes: Acquired by Orijin; the site announces the combination into an education-to-employment pathway. Buyer mix is split between public agencies and private employers paying to post fair-chance roles. Crunchbase lists Columbus, OH; their own About page gives an Austin, TX address, which I used.

description: Contingency management and recovery support software for substance use treatment providers, and PARCA supervision tools for probation and parole agencies
notes: Straddles two categories: the criminal-justice product PARCA is why they exhibited at APPA, but the larger product line is behavioral health treatment software.

description: Water data management and regulatory compliance software for water utilities, cities and environmental agencies
notes: Operates as Aquatic Informatics ULC under Veralto Water Quality; acquired by Danaher in 2020 and carried into the Veralto spin-off. Products include Aquarius, WIMS, WaterTrax, Linko and Tokay.

description: After-hours call intake, incident triage and crew dispatch software for water, sewer and electric utilities and public works departments
notes: Category is a compromise: Daupler RMS is cross-departmental (water, sewer, stormwater, electric, general public works), and water/sewer is its largest market. Founding year from Crunchbase and the KCRise Fund portfolio page, not the company site.

description: IoT sensor and AI wastewater monitoring platform that traces upstream pollution events for water authorities and treatment plants
notes: Sells IoT hardware alongside the analytics platform. Founding year from Israeli startup press and Startup Nation Central, not the company's own about page.

description: Reinforcement learning control software that automatically optimizes chemical dosing and process settings at drinking water and wastewater plants
notes: The homepage is written generically about 'plants'; water and wastewater is confirmed as the actual market by their December 2024 $5M seed announcement (led by TQ Ventures) and WaterWorld coverage of deployments at three Alberta and BC plants. No founding year found.

description: Cloud SCADA monitoring, alarming and analytics software for water and wastewater utilities, treatment plants and lift stations
notes: Part of the MANN+HUMMEL Group. No founding year found on their about page or in Crunchbase.

description: Subscription online training and CEU tracking platform for water and wastewater operators pursuing state licensure
notes: HQ omitted deliberately: the .us site states no location, and ZoomInfo lists a Neuilly-sur-Seine, France address, which I could not corroborate against the US-facing business. Judgment call on verdict: this is a training-content subscription rather than an operational system, but it is delivered as a licensed e-learning platform, not a services engagement.

description: Registered apprenticeship and work-based learning management software for state workforce agencies, community colleges, school districts and employer sponsors
notes: Acquired by WGU Labs in September 2024 and now runs as a nonprofit operating division of Western Governors University under the retained Craft Education name. HQ and founding year are from PitchBook and the WGU acquisition press, not the current site.

description: Cybersecurity program management and NIST CSF compliance platform for county governments and critical infrastructure agencies
notes: HQ omitted: their own site gives no address, and ZoomInfo/The Org list only the region 'Lehigh Valley, PA' rather than a city, which does not meet the City, ST format. description: Child support lien network, new hire reporting and Medicaid recovery web systems for state child support and labor agencies
notes: Their own site describes the company as a web systems builder for government, so part of the engagement is custom development; the lien network and new hire reporting products are recurring systems, which is why this reads as product rather than services.

description: IT help desk ticketing, device asset management and facilities service software built for K-12 school districts
notes: Backed by JMI Equity (2021) and Cove Hill Partners (2024). Founded August 2016 per company and investor press; the platform launched publicly at ISTE 2017, so some sources cite 2017.

description: Classroom browser monitoring, web filtering and student wellbeing alerting software for K-12 schools and districts
notes: Now a business unit of Cordance Operations LLC, which is why the HQ reads Raleigh rather than the company's original New Zealand base. Founding year omitted: the only on-site signal is a '2010-' copyright range, which is not a stated founding date.

description: Free keyboarding, digital citizenship and AI literacy curriculum for K-12 schools, with a paid ad-free district edition
